title: Néron models and semistable abelian varieties, Part II: genus-one fibrations and rational elliptic surfaces
summary: Extend the regular-model and component-group theory to genus-one fibrations over curves, finite-field nonsplit fibers and geometrically rational Jacobian surfaces. General Ferrand pinching supplies reusable conductor squares; excellent-DVR multiple fibers, global Weierstrass equations, Picard constancy and a corrected fourteen-model F₂ classification form the application chain. All classification conclusions retain an explicit completeness certificate. The finite five-curve F₂ coefficient classification has an explicit sixteen-row witness table; scheme-presentation exports and the surface-model completeness certificate remain distinct inputs. This partial checkpoint supplies actual k-linear quadratic-pinch coordinates, a native transported Basis and coefficient/degree interfaces; the complete presentation and normalization remain open. The quadratic affine chart now includes its full native substitution kernel and canonical quotient algebra comparison; geometric closure remains open. The actual ring comparison away from a common-ideal element permits a noninjective original map; every polynomial pinch has its explicit localized coordinate inverse. The specified native affine A_q-linear B/(A_q·1)≃E/(A_q·1), its actual k-linear B/A_q≃E/k, both representative equations, residue scalar actions, one-dimensional quadratic defect and actual conductor annihilators are now separately checked prototypes. Projective chart gluing, the global normalization comparison, conductor ideal sheaf, the actual structure-sheaf sequence and finite-pushforward H0/H1 remain open, as does the independent I₂ geometry. The full Tau Ceti-importing file is uncompiled; all implementation statuses and all seven coverage rows remain partial/unchecked. The reciprocal infinity quotient Chart(a,b)=R[u][Z]/(Q∞Z−u³), its explicit Bézout inverse, both specified R[u]-algebra maps and their inverse equivalence, native localization property and actual affine Spec open immersion now have separately checked prototypes over every commutative ring. The homogeneous normalization tuple, its cubic homogeneity and fieldwise absence of a common zero are checked against the actual native projective Weierstrass equation, with a nonsingular infinity point over every field. The two-chart overlap/gluing and actual Proj comparison, finite projective normalization, conductor ideal sheaf, structure-sheaf exact sequence, finite-pushforward H0/H1 and independent I₂ geometry remain required. Full Tau Ceti-importing file remains uncompiled; all seven stages are partial and all mathematical implementation statuses unchecked. For every field k and q=t²+at+b, the specified finite global map ν:N→C is surjective; both schemes are integral, every source stalk is integrally closed, and an actual dense-open Scheme.PartialIso agrees with ν over Spec k. The projective-line and Proj identifications, normalization universal property, projectivity/properness, conductor ideal sheaf, structure-sheaf exact sequence and finite-pushforward H0/H1 remain separate obligations. The I₂ construction and all other inherited gaps remain open; seven stages stay partial and all implementations unchecked. For every field k and q=t²+at+b, the existing affine pinch A_q has the actual native k[T]-algebra action T↦q and an injective parameter map. The existing coordinates upgrade to a k[T]-linear equivalence k[T]²≃A_q, with native finite basis {1,tq}, exact polynomial coefficients and two-term reconstruction. The specified module is free, finite, of finrank2 and flat over k[q]. These properties concern the quadratic parameter algebra. Projective-line/Proj identifications, normalization universal property, conductor sheaves, coherent cohomology and independent I₂ geometry remain required. All seven stages remain partial and every implementation remains unchecked. For every nonempty affine U⊂C, the actual B_U=Γ(N,ν⁻¹U) is integrally closed and is the integral closure of A_U=Γ(C,U) in K_N. The specified σ upgrades to an A_U-algebra equivalence and gives E_U:B_U≃integralClosure(A_U,K_C), with exact forward/inverse generic-germ, coefficient and restriction laws. This settles the affine generic-field comparison. It does not identify E_U with the sections of the existing δ: compare against native normalizationDiagram/normalizationObjIso, handle the empty-open branch and assemble the scheme isomorphism. Preserve P¹/Proj identification, properness/projectivity, conductor ideal sheaf and exact sequence, finite-pushforward H0/H1 and the independent I₂ geometry. All seven stages remain partial and every implementation unchecked. Twelve native-normalization section nodes (three constructions and nine lemmas) give κ_U:S_U≃ₐ[A_U]K_C for nonempty U, θ_U:D_U≃ₐ[A_U]integralClosure(A_U,K_C) and Ψ_U:D_U≃ₐ[A_U]B_U for nonempty affine U, with exact coefficients, ambient values, inverse formulas and κ restriction compatibility. General rational-function and normalization APIs are imported. Identification with δ.app, θ/Ψ restriction compatibility, empty opens and global scheme assembly remain required. The resulting packet has 513 nodes; all stages remain partial and all implementations unchecked. The actual comparison δ:η.normalization→N is now identified with Ψ_U⁻¹ on nonempty affine sections, with native closure and source restriction formulas. Empty-open sections are handled separately, the finite-map affine cover proves δ is a scheme isomorphism, and its inverse respects both triangles. The actual comparison upgrades to Λ_U:B_U≃ₐ[A_U]D_U on every open, commuting with forward and inverse restriction and the actual coefficients; on nonempty affine opens it recovers Ψ_U⁻¹. The native projective-line/Proj identifications, properness/projectivity, conductor ideal sheaf and structure-sheaf exact sequence, finite-pushforward H0/H1, independent I₂ geometry and every inherited family/model/classification obligation remain required. All seven stages are partial and every mathematical implementation status is unchecked. The full canonical Tau Ceti-importing file is uncompiled; the bounded Mathlib artifacts with the consumed exact pinned Tau Ceti source excerpt are checked. The common-ideal reconstruction now has native comparison, kernel, compatible-pair lifting and categorical pullback proofs, an actual inverse-coordinate ring equivalence, and an additive sequence whose middle exactness is equivalent to the image being an ideal. The arbitrary-subring conductor square and native quotient-module annihilator identity are checked separately, and actual all-open conductor ideals agree across the absolute normalization isomorphism. The conductor ideal sheaf, structure-sheaf sequence, properness/projectivity and cohomology remain separate obligations.
readme: This Part II begins after R11.2 and R11.4 and imports the existing StableReduction and EllipticCurves layers. The companion reader gives exact conventions, declaration contracts, API and tests. It does not prove the Enriques nonexistence theorem. The published eleven-model enumeration is replaced by fourteen candidates, with individual model verification separated from exhaustiveness.

stages.title: Ferrand pinching and conductor squares
stages.description: For a closed immersion Z→Y and finite map Z→Z′, define the geometric square by the topological quotient and the pullback of structure sheaves. Prove affine existence using the existing ring pullback, its cartesian property, finiteness, complement isomorphism and flat base change. For global schemes assume each finite fiber of Z→Z′ has an affine neighbourhood in Y (Ferrand 7.1); the stronger (AF) hypothesis is a convenient corollary. General conductor ideals and nodal/cuspidal pinching examples are included. The universal-homeomorphism restriction matches Witaszek 2.17; his topological predicate alone is not a categorical pushout. Independently of this scheme criterion, every finite pinching datum of algebraic spaces over a scheme base is effective by Temkin–Tyomkin5.3.1(ii),6.2.1(ii)(b), with no Noetherian or quasi-separated assumption. Decompose the compatible étale cover, affine universality against spaces, overlap, relation quotient, cartesian/sheaf/finite/closed properties, flat comparison and the if-and-only-if scheme-recognition criterion. Exact SF.1/SF.3 exports and the full space signatures remain partial. The global Scheme conductor extension uses the native IdealSheafData/subscheme/comapIso carriers, with finite schematically dominant hypotheses; reduced Noetherian finite-surjective maps are its source specialization. Separate the specialized annihilator, finite flat/localization, quotient-chart and geometric/categorical comparisons. Flat base change recomputes the same conductor, including nilpotents; nonflat base change is excluded. The generic finite-module annihilator formula is an SF.0 request. Specify the actual native common-ideal localization equivalence for arbitrary commutative rings, using image-ideal and kernel-intersection hypotheses rather than injectivity of the original map; retain the inverse fraction and nilpotent tests. The common-ideal reconstruction now has native comparison, kernel, compatible-pair lifting and categorical pullback proofs, an actual inverse-coordinate ring equivalence, and an additive sequence whose middle exactness is equivalent to the image being an ideal. The arbitrary-subring conductor square and native quotient-module annihilator identity are checked separately, and actual all-open conductor ideals agree across the absolute normalization isomorphism. The conductor ideal sheaf, structure-sheaf sequence, properness/projectivity and cohomology remain separate obligations. The finite spanning-family conductor criterion, product common-denominator equivalence and native fraction membership in its extended ideal retain arbitrary commutative bases, noninjective coefficient maps, empty families and nilpotent denominators. The recomputed localized-B conductor and global IdealSheafData restriction comparisons remain separate required identifications; no stage closes. The actual finite-algebra conductor is now recomputed after localization, with no injectivity or denominator-regularity assumption. Six new supporting declarations and four regression tests specialize the previous finite-generator checkpoint; the global affine-restriction/IdealSheafData comparison remains open. The actual conductor family now satisfies the native basic-open compatibility law; ofIdeals preserves every prescribed affine ideal. Native proofs establish the old membership, greatest-ideal and affine ofIdealTop contracts, arbitrary affine restriction and composition, identity and empty-open boundaries, the canonical ΓSpecIso comparison, and the affine quotient-module annihilator formula. The native closed subscheme is available, with the identity case checked empty. Still construct and compare the conductor quotient-square maps, the all-open structure-sheaf exact sequence and categorical geometric pushout, the recomputed flat base-change comparison, projectivity/properness/cohomology and the remaining I2 and other routed-paper targets. The generic flat-annihilator supplier request remains open. The full Tau-importing canonical file remains uncompiled; no whole-stage completion is claimed. The actual conductorMap now has checked native square, cartesian and finite APIs, comparison with subschemeMap and uniqueness. Its actual section map is defined on every target open and commutes with native restrictions. On affine opens, the two actual subschemeObjIso identifications conjugate this section map to the native induced quotient-ring map A/I→B/J, where J is the actual pulled-back ideal datum. The nonreduced diagonal Z/4 example retains a nonzero square-zero class on both sides and shows the induced map need not be an isomorphism. The exact equality J(V)=c(im(f.app U),B) still requires the affine tensor-quotient/pullback ideal comparison; no geometric pushout or all-open structure-sheaf exactness is inferred. All inherited properness/projectivity, P¹/Proj, cohomology, flat-recomputed conductor, I2 and classification obligations remain required. All seven stages remain partial and every implementation unchecked; the full Tau-importing suggested file remains uncompiled.

stages.title: Genus-one fibers and finite-field forms
stages.description:
Extend the imported smooth-curve minimal models to regular relatively minimal genus-one fibrations over a smooth proper curve, including quasielliptic generic fibers. Distinguish gcd multiplicity, the indecomposable divisor and the reduced subscheme. Define geometric Kodaira realization using the upstream equation-side symbols, with intersection and field-of-definition data. Construct nonsplit I₁ and I₂ over finite fields by pinching. Prove rational-component incidence counts and the five F₂ elliptic isomorphism classes. Supply the native F₂ five-model family, binary discriminant branches, all sixteen smooth coefficient tuples and explicit forward triples in the eight-element native VariableChange group, their distinct projective counts and cyclic point-group generators. Keep the SF.3 pointed scheme/Weierstrass presentation and infinity-preserving comparison distinct from rational point-group isomorphism. The quadratic-pinching continuation derives the affine subalgebra and hypersurface, conductor and finite normalization, proper single-point existence, the two cohomology quotients and odd/even finite-extension counts. General node/cohomology carriers remain imported from StableReduction and SF.3; characteristic2 inseparable tangents and component-permuting I₂ forms are not identified with the separable fixed-component case. Its affine quadratic chart has native k-linear polynomial-pair coordinates and a transported monomial-product Basis with exact coefficients and degrees; the native full substitution range/kernel and canonical bivariate quotient algebra comparison are now explicitly planned and separately prototyped. Finite normalization, fraction-field, projective and cohomology comparisons remain open. For every polynomial q, the native pinch inclusion becomes bijective after inverting q, with inverse coordinate(qX)/q; finite normalization and projective/sheaf comparisons are separate targets. The native affine normalization continuation specifies actual A_q module coefficients, span{1,X}=top, finite inclusion and the finite native Spec map, a shared fraction field for all nonzero q with inverse coordinate(qX)/q, and the actual integral closure for monic quadratics. The coefficient pair has a nonzero relation and is not a module basis; no flatness is asserted. Complete the projective two-chart and scheme-normalization comparison before conductor ideal sheaves and finite-pushforward cohomology. The specified native affine A_q-linear B/(A_q·1)≃E/(A_q·1), its actual k-linear B/A_q≃E/k, both representative equations, residue scalar actions, one-dimensional quadratic defect and actual conductor annihilators are now separately checked prototypes. Projective chart gluing, the global normalization comparison, conductor ideal sheaf, the actual structure-sheaf sequence and finite-pushforward H0/H1 remain open, as does the independent I₂ geometry. The full Tau Ceti-importing file is uncompiled; all implementation statuses and all seven coverage rows remain partial/unchecked.

The homogeneous normalization tuple, its cubic homogeneity and fieldwise absence of a common zero are checked against the actual native projective Weierstrass equation, with a nonsingular infinity point over every field. The two-chart overlap/gluing and actual Proj comparison, finite projective normalization, conductor ideal sheaf, structure-sheaf exact sequence, finite-pushforward H0/H1 and independent I₂ geometry remain required. Full Tau Ceti-importing file remains uncompiled; all seven stages are partial and all mathematical implementation statuses unchecked.

**Overlap comparison.** The specified reciprocal polynomial localization equivalence is checked over arbitrary commutative rings, with its actual affine Spec isomorphism. The finite pinch localization at tq is identified with the normalized overlap; the infinity quotient localization at u is identified with the reversed polynomial overlap, and D(z)=D(u) is proved in its actual prime spectrum. Their composite gives the specified chart transition, and the homogeneous normalization tuples agree by the unit factor t⁻³. The global Proj identification, gluing of the normalization morphism, projective finiteness, conductor ideal sheaf, structure-sheaf exact sequence, finite-pushforward H0/H1 and separate I₂ geometry remain required. All stages remain partial and implementation statuses unchecked; the full Tau Ceti-importing file is uncompiled.

**Native two-chart schemes.** The actual quadratic two-chart Scheme C and glued source N, their coefficient-compatible global morphism ν, both target-chart pullback squares, and global finiteness of ν have separately checked native prototypes. The actual overlap map has u=1/t and z=1/(tq). Identify C with the specified Proj cubic and N with the native projective line, prove the normalization universal property and projectivity/properness, then identify the conductor ideal sheaf and structure-sheaf exact sequence and derive finite-pushforward H0/H1. Separate I₂ geometry and all other inherited obligations remain required; all stages stay partial and all implementations unchecked. For every field k and q=t²+at+b, the specified finite global map ν:N→C is surjective; both schemes are integral, every source stalk is integrally closed, and an actual dense-open Scheme.PartialIso agrees with ν over Spec k. The projective-line and Proj identifications, normalization universal property, projectivity/properness, conductor ideal sheaf, structure-sheaf exact sequence and finite-pushforward H0/H1 remain separate obligations. The I₂ construction and all other inherited gaps remain open; seven stages stay partial and all implementations unchecked. For every field k and q=t²+at+b, the existing affine pinch A_q has the actual native k[T]-algebra action T↦q and an injective parameter map. The existing coordinates upgrade to a k[T]-linear equivalence k[T]²≃A_q, with native finite basis {1,tq}, exact polynomial coefficients and two-term reconstruction. The specified module is free, finite, of finrank2 and flat over k[q]. These properties concern the quadratic parameter algebra. Projective-line/Proj identifications, normalization universal property, conductor sheaves, coherent cohomology and independent I₂ geometry remain required. All seven stages remain partial and every implementation remains unchecked.

**Affine absolute integral closure.** For every nonempty affine U⊂C, the actual B_U=Γ(N,ν⁻¹U) is integrally closed and is the integral closure of A_U=Γ(C,U) in K_N. The specified σ upgrades to an A_U-algebra equivalence and gives E_U:B_U≃integralClosure(A_U,K_C), with exact forward/inverse generic-germ, coefficient and restriction laws. This settles the affine generic-field comparison. It does not identify E_U with the sections of the existing δ: compare against native normalizationDiagram/normalizationObjIso, handle the empty-open branch and assemble the scheme isomorphism. Preserve P¹/Proj identification, properness/projectivity, conductor ideal sheaf and exact sequence, finite-pushforward H0/H1 and the independent I₂ geometry. Construct the actual native normalization section equivalences through the existing rational-function API and native normalizationObjIso, using the actual coefficient actions. Compare them with δ on affine sections, prove restriction compatibility, handle empty opens and assemble the scheme identification before deriving conductor-sheaf and cohomology statements. The actual comparison δ:η.normalization→N is now identified with Ψ_U⁻¹ on nonempty affine sections, with native closure and source restriction formulas. Empty-open sections are handled separately, the finite-map affine cover proves δ is a scheme isomorphism, and its inverse respects both triangles. The actual comparison upgrades to Λ_U:B_U≃ₐ[A_U]D_U on every open, commuting with forward and inverse restriction and the actual coefficients; on nonempty affine opens it recovers Ψ_U⁻¹. stages.title: Multiple fibers over excellent discrete valuation rings
stages.description: Prove the regular-model adapters in Schröer 8.1–8.3: the transverse horizontal DVR divisor has reduced intersection Spec k but schematic fiber length m; normalize its base change, lift the section, verify Raynaud (N)*, and obtain cohomological flatness, h⁰=1 and h¹=1 from χ=0. Construct the reduced-fiber isogeny, deduce all finite extension counts and the F₂ isomorphism. Use LLR 6.6 only with algebraically closed residue field and retain its hypotheses; finite-field nonsplit descent is a separate result.

stages.title: Rational Jacobians and global Weierstrass equations
stages.description: For a geometrically rational Jacobian genus-one surface over P¹, construct the relative cubic by contracting vertical components, prove the splitting of f_*O(3O), and obtain deg aᵢ≤i with the inverse chart s=1/t and aᵢ′=sⁱaᵢ(1/s). Prove the rational-surface Picard/intersection realization: rank10, odd unimodular signature(1,9), the unimodular fiber/section plane, and its even negative-definite rank8 complement. Import the abstract IntegralLattice API. State quasielliptic characteristic restrictions and canonical bundle/tame-wild corrections.

stages.title: Picard constancy and fiber configurations
stages.description: Prove the genus-one generic Picard restriction with vertical kernel. For a rational Jacobian surface over F₂, state all five conditions of Schröer 9.4, including descent of geometric Mordell–Weil sections and the fiber point sum25. Prove the corrected graph rigidity of 9.5, treat IV as a triangle and distinguish all three terminal multiplicities of III* and II*. Relate Picard constancy to #J(F₂)=25 using geometric cycle classes and Frobenius. Prove the large-fiber, additive-fiber and uniqueness constraints with the singularity assumption Δ=0 kept in the c₄ test.

stages.title: Fourteen explicit models over F₂
stages.description: Specify and verify fourteen bounded Weierstrass models: eleven with nonzero j and three with j=0. Include the three omitted equations as separate model certificates. For each, prove global minimality, geometric rationality, all rational fiber types and splitting data, and the resolved-surface count25. Include the degree-two bad fibers of models2 and14. Generic cubic point counts alone do not certify the surface. Isomorphism classifications and exhaustiveness belong to G.6.

stages.title: Completeness and classification certificates
stages.description: Prove that every relatively minimal geometrically rational Jacobian elliptic surface over P¹_F₂ with constant Picard scheme is equivalent to one of the fourteen verified models, under admissible Weierstrass changes and PGL₂(F₂). Separate the 2²¹ bounded coefficient search (2¹⁸ after the proved a₂=0 normalization), the 512 coordinate transformations, all-place minimality, and rational double-point resolution/counting from the exhaustiveness conclusion. Acquire William Lang (2000) before using its conductor/configuration exclusions, or certify a complete finite search including every rejection. The classifications are conditional on that explicit certificate until it is proved.
